Prevention: Select and plant loose or open head sorghum varieties because they are rarely attacked by the bollworm.
Deep ploughing in off-season to expose the pupae of bollworm in the soil to sunlight and natural enemies.
Monitoring: The larvae feed on the sorghum head, monitor for bollworm larvae from head emergence to grain fill once in a week.
Look for larvae ranging from about 1 cm (small size) to about 4 cm (fully grown larvae) on the sorghum head.
Choose five different points in ¼ hectare, check 6-10 sorghum heads by beating heads to dislodge the larvae onto a sheet or onto the ground.
In addition, look for sheared developing grain, and frass in leaf axils and into tight compacted head.
Consider control measures when larvae are seen on 5 to 10 % of the sampled plant heads.
The crop is considered heavily damaged when the larvae reach older stage (35-40 mm) and if the infestation is high.
Direct Control: Shaking the plants to induce the larvae to drop into a bucket or other appropriate materials; handpick and kill/crush larvae, in small fields.
Larvae on open panicles are exposed to predaceous insects and birds.
Spray on foliar and sorghum head with lambda-cyhalothrin (contact pyrethroids).
